hook.text: A restaurant reservation app at 3 AM has zero liquidity. At 7 PM, it's bursting with demand.

buildup.text: Some marketplaces have liquidity that varies by time of day, day of week, or season.

discovery.text: Uber uses surge pricing to solve temporal liquidity: higher prices lure more drivers during peak demand.

twist.text: eBay auctions ending on Sunday evenings get 15% higher prices. Timing affects marketplace economics.

climax.text: Smart marketplaces match supply scheduling with demand patterns to maximize liquidity at all times.

punchline.text: 7 PM: everyone wants a table. 3 AM: nobody does. Timing is liquidity.

quiz.question: How does Uber address time-based liquidity problems?
options: Surge pricing to attract drivers during peak demand

details.summary: Time-based liquidity measures how quickly a marketplace can match supply with demand. Markets for perishable inventory like hotel rooms, restaurant reservations, and ride-sharing need real-time matching, while durable goods like used cars can tolerate longer match times without losing value.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding time sensitivity determines marketplace design. Real-time markets need instant matching algorithms and always-on supply..
takeaways: Perishable inventory requires real-time matching before value expires completely
Durable goods markets tolerate longer match times and prioritize match quality
Time pressure creates different marketplace designs for different inventory types

faq.question: How does inventory perishability affect marketplace design?
faq.answer: An empty hotel room tonight is worthless tomorrow. This time pressure drives aggressive last-minute pricing and instant booking capabilities. A used car maintains value for months, enabling careful listing, negotiation, and inspection..

faq.question: Which marketplace categories face the most severe time-based liquidity challenges?
faq.answer: Ride-sharing needs matches within minutes. Food delivery within 30 to 60 minutes. Event tickets before the date. Fresh grocery delivery within hours. These all require dense, always-available supply and sophisticated real-time dispatch algorithms to function effectively.
